You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The test `testAddNonComparable` tries to add a plain Object instance (`new Object()`) to a Frequency instance by calling `addValue(Object)`. According to the current bug report, the expectation is that this should not be allowed because only Comparable objects should be added. The test expects a `ClassCastException` to be thrown, but the issue report states that it wasn't initially (comment `// This was OK`), causing the instance's internal state to be corrupted in a way that a subsequent add fails with an `IllegalArgumentException`.

Looking at the `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method implementation, it is marked as `@Deprecated`. It accepts an Object parameter and uses a `TreeMap` (initialized in the constructor) to store frequencies. The code tries to retrieve the current count for the value from the `freqTable`. If the object is an Integer, it converts it to Long first, presumably to standardize keys. The critical part is the catch block for `ClassCastException` thrown by `freqTable.get(obj)`. The code translates this to an `IllegalArgumentException` with the message "Value not comparable to existing values."

This means that the method `addValue(Object)` itself does not explicitly check that `v` is Comparable before adding it; it relies on the TreeMap to throw `ClassCastException` if `v` is not comparable to existing keys. This causes inconsistency because the first addition of a plain Object instance (not comparable) is accepted without exception, but the internal TreeMap (which requires keys to be mutually comparable) will fail in subsequent operations.

The root problem is that `addValue(Object)` should reject any input that is not an instance of Comparable right away to prevent adding non-comparable keys to the TreeMap, instead of relying on TreeMap's behavior to raise exception later. The current test exposing this issue by adding a plain Object without causing an exception in the first call but expecting a failure (ClassCastException) highlights this bug.

Hence, the bug occurs because `addValue(Object)` lacks an explicit check enforcing that added values must implement Comparable before insertion. This leads to inconsistent internal state and unexpected `IllegalArgumentException` in later operations.

Recent bug reports retrieved are not relevant for this diagnosis as they are not related to this API or similar issues.

This analysis aligns with the current report's comment that "the first call to addValue(Object) which should not allow a plain Object to be added - it should only allow Comparable objects." The current behavior of `addValue(Object)` accepts such an addition without immediate failure, causing the regression and test failure.

---

Suggested fix location is in the `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method to enforce input validation for Comparable objects before insertion into the frequency table.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
